name: Netflix
notice: A layout study, not Netflix: Netflix's signed-out pages rebuilt with Golden Grids as GIFflix, a parody name, using public-domain films. Not affiliated with Netflix; the service and its plans are fictional.
summary: Netflix's signed-out home page and a title page, rebuilt as stacked golden grids around twelve films of Weimar cinema. A ranked row of ten becomes two grids in which rank sets size, and one film is opened scene by scene.

reviewed.method: Captured signed out at 390, 820 and 1440 pixels. The signed-in browse page redirects to a login and was not captured. The pages are named here but not linked: a page styled after a streaming service that links to that service reads as phishing to Google's scanners, which flagged the address these studies share in October 2026. The repository's README links them.

pages.label: A Netflix title page, signed out

real: The twelve films, 1920 to 1929, with their years and directors. All are in the public domain in the United States, where this study is hosted; six appear to remain protected in Germany.
The stills and clips, which are frames from those films.
invented: GIFflix as a streaming service, with its plans, prices, reasons to join and questions. The name is a parody made for this study; none of it exists.
The ranking of the ten films, the synopses and every caption.
The closing band, which says that GIFflix has no accounts. The reference's membership form and the header's account control are left out, so nothing on the page asks the reader for anything.

assets.source: Cut from prints on the Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons (captures/stills.sh in the source records each one). Some prints are restorations of uncertain origin.
